sermon.title: Stupid and Twisted on the Edge
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from 2 Peter 3:16 and 2 Peter 2 about “untaught” and “unstable” people who twist the scriptures. He lists doctrines he says are twisted, including once saved always saved, the prosperity doctrine, purgatory and infant baptism, discusses who interprets scripture, and says believers should be like the Bereans and search the Bible daily.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: he says “Matthew 22:28” for the passage about marriage in heaven (Matthew 22:30), and “Hebrews 12 or one two,” meaning Hebrews 1:1-2. “Second Peter 3:. 16” and other references are as spoken in the captions. Some caption slips are corrected where the intended word is clear (for example “cooks” to “kooks” and “meth” to “medicine”), and three spots with garbled names of well-known preachers are marked [unclear]. This message contains strong statements about homosexuality, Catholic teaching, Jehovah’s Witnesses, Jews, “liberal Christians,” well-known preachers and a TV host, medicine and faith, and using a gun to protect a family; these are his own views and are not verified here, and the names stay in the transcript only.

chunks.section_question: How do false teachers entice people, and what is “liberty” that enslaves? (2 Peter 2:14, 2 Peter 2:19)
chunks.short_answer: He says false teachers tell people “they can sin and still have eternal life,” which is what “seducing” and “entice” means, to “make sin look attractive and make sin look approved and okay.” He says God does not make anyone a homosexual or a thief: “you chose to do that,” and describes visiting a church in Paraguay that stopped bringing the Bible and waited for the Holy Ghost, which he calls “their own imagination.”
chunks.text:
Number four, they want to hear that they can sin and still have eternal life. That’s the bottom line. Okay, “they speak evil of things they do not understand, they will utterly perish in their own corruption, they’ll receive the wages of unrighteousness, having eyes full of adultery,” verse 14, “that cannot cease from sin, enticing unstable souls.” Seducing. Now here it is. Who are these people following false prophets and buying false information and and wanting to live in sin? what How does he title them? Unstable. The very scripture he says, “unlearned and unstable people twist the scriptures to their own destruction.” So this, the word “entice” means to seduce, make sin look attractive and make sin look approved and okay. Yeah, and that’s what ministers are telling the homosexuals, “Oh, it’s okay, God made you that way.” That’s a lie. God didn’t make a pedophile a pedophile, a thief a thief, or a homosexual a homosexual. You chose to do that.

Number five, “they boast of having liberty, but they are the slave slaves of destruction.” “Oh, I’m mature now. I used to believe like you, but I’m mature now.” Oh, I was down in a church in Paraguay where they didn’t even bring the Bible to church anymore. They just let the Holy Spirit teach them. Us Spirit-filled people can be kooks. I tell you, we can be really kooks. The Bible says to study to show thyself approved. “Seek ye out of the book of the law and read.” The Bible says these things. chunks.section_question: Which desires are okay, and what happens when people who knew the way go back? (2 Peter 2:18-21)
chunks.short_answer: He says desires to eat, for sexual fulfillment and to relax are given by God, but “lewdness” means going overboard, and “you don’t have to be stupid” because you have a desire. He reads 2 Peter 2:20-21 that if they are again entangled and overcome “the latter end is worse for them than the beginning,” and says it is horrible for someone to think they are okay when they are not.
chunks.text:
second Peter 2:18: “They speak great boastful words of emptiness, they entice to the lust of the flesh, lewdness.” It’s important that lewdness is there, because there are desires of the flesh that are okay. You’ll have a desire to eat, there’s nothing wrong with that. You’ll have a desire for sexual fulfillment, there’s nothing wrong with that. God put it there, you understand? You’ll have a desire to relax and enjoy, have a recreational time. God gave us that. But he put the word “lewd,” evil, in there, so you know that when you go overboard or you break away from what’s right, that’s the wrong desire. Okay, that’s very important. And a lot of people beat themselves up, you know, looking at a woman and lust after her. “Oh my my God, oh my God, oh my God.” Look, God created you a sexual being. Relax. Just control it, bridle it. You don’t have to drink arsenic, you can drink milk. You don’t have to eat poison or whatever, or poison ivy, you can eat wholesome food. You don’t have to be stupid. Just because you got a desire to eat doesn’t mean you don’t have the faculties to control what you eat, does it?

Number six, they had escaped the way of righteousness, knew the way of right, but turned back and were entangled and overcome. And that’s what he says in verse 20, “after escaping the pollutions of the world by the knowledge of the Lord Jesus Christ.” See, that’s why we need to go a church where they’re teaching us knowledge, they’re teaching us wisdom, they’re giving us things that work. “They are again entangled in those things they were saved from and overcome, the latter end is worse for them than the beginning.” Why? Because now they think they’re going to heaven, and they’re not. And it’s horrible when somebody thinks they’re okay when they’re not okay. Verse 21: “It would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness.” So they see, they knew the way of righteousness, and they left it, and “after knowing it, to turn from that holy commandment delivered to them.” Now folks, I’ve watched a lot of people turn. I’ve watched them touch God, I’ve watched God save them, I watched them commit themselves to living for God and repenting from their sin and stopping sinning, and then somebody comes along and, that and uh you understand me, and we bond, we connect, and they teach them lies, and they get in a little clique, and they fall away. I’ve seen it over and over and over.

chunks.section_question: How should we respond? Be like the Bereans (Acts 17:11, Matthew 7:16, 2 Peter 2:22)
chunks.short_answer: He quotes “a dog returns to his own vomit” for those who go back to sin, and says twisted doctrine destroys people and “all of us are guilty.” He says Peter wrote to genuine Christians to watch for unstable teachers, and we should search the scriptures daily like the Bereans, look for Jesus in every book, and know people by their fruit, since “denomination doesn’t save you.”
chunks.text:
But it has happened to them according to the true proverb: “A dog returns to his own vomit, and a pig after being washed to her wallowing in the mire.” So the unstable go back to sin, or they never really come out. Hallelujah. I’ve seen a lot of things, church. Twisted doctrine destroys people. The Catholics, the Baptists, the Presbyterians, all of us are guilty. And it’s our fault that we believe a church doctrine of faith above the Bible and not know what the Bible says ourself. That’s our fault. Hallelujah. How many going to raise your hand and said, “Man, I’m going to watch out for twisted doctrine”? Yes. You know, it’s easy for us to do it. we want to say we want to We want the scripture so badly to back up what we believe that we twist it. It’s important for you to know who Peter wrote this to. Okay, who did Peter write these words to? He wrote him to those who obtain the same precious faith as him and others by Jesus Christ. The same faith we’re supposed to have. The same faith Jesus had, the same faith the apostles had, equal faith, you can’t change it. We got to have the same faith. Amen. And that’s who he wrote to. He said, you people, be careful of unstable and unlearned people that twist the scriptures. And he’s writing to you, if you’re a genuine Christian that wants to serve Christ. You may have problems in your life, but you’re working on him, you’re growing. He’s writing to you and say, watch out for these unlearned and unstable people that twist the scriptures, that give you liberty to stay in the sin you’re in or go back to the sin.

This is the kind of people we got to be, the Bereans. They “receive the word with all readiness of mind and they search the scriptures.” How often? Daily. To see whether those things were true. Those things Paul and Peter and them were teaching them, they search the scriptures daily. You cannot be a Bible scholar going to church once or twice a week and just getting a message from your pastor. You got to get into the word daily. And God promised to open that word up to you, and let me tell you the key. The key is he wants to reveal Jesus. So when you start reading Genesis, who do you look for? Jesus. When you read Leviticus, that boring book, who you looking for? Jesus. Hallelujah. The truth. Matthew 7:16: “You shall know them by their” what? Fruit. Not by their mouth, by their lifestyle, by how they live. Anybody can say, “I believe in Jesus.” A disciple follows him. Amen. A disciple isn’t tripped up by these winds of doctrine, these twisted people. We must not disregard true Bible doctrines. We must not twist scriptures to our own and others’ destruction. I may will raise your right hand and say, “Yes, I agree with that. That’s truth. I mustn’t. I must be very careful.”

Yes. Doesn’t matter what denomination we’re in, denomination doesn’t save you. Jesus and the word saves you. We must not leave the way of truth and right by inventing our own beliefs, using twisted scripture. Wow. How many’s been guilty of inventing your own doctrines in days past? Man, I’m I was guilty. What my biggest mistake as a young Christian, I believed everything they said on the radio, and boy, I found out the hard way they were lying. I mean really, they were lying. That’s flat out lies. They were just flat out lying. So I learned not to follow those people on the radio. I turned off the radio and turned on the Bible tapes. I started listening to Paul and Peter and these guys.

faqs.question: What does he say “twist” means?
faqs.answer: He says “twist means to distort, to explain falsely, to misinterpret,” and to change the meaning of scripture.

scriptures.text_nkjv: as also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things, in which are some things hard to understand, which untaught and unstable people twist to their own destruction, as they do also the rest of the Scriptures.

faqs.question: What does he say about “once saved always saved”?
faqs.answer: He says it “is not in the Bible anywhere,” and cites God telling Moses “he that sins will I blot out of my book,” which he says shows those in the book could be blotted out.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And the LORD said to Moses, “Whoever has sinned against Me, I will blot him out of My book.

faqs.question: Does he say Jesus drank wine?
faqs.answer: He says “nowhere in the Bible does it say Jesus drank wine,” and that at the communion table Jesus said “I will not drink of this cup till I drink it with you in the kingdom.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: for I say to you, I will not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.”

faqs.question: Is the Bible a book of faith or a book of truth?
faqs.answer: He says “nowhere in the Bible does it say the Bible’s a book of faith,” and that it is “a book of truth” which can be used in any debate, including science and politics.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Sanctify them by Your truth. Your word is truth.

faqs.question: What does he say science means?
faqs.answer: He says “science just means knowledge. That’s all. It’s not some magic word that makes a scientist a guru.”

faqs.question: What does he say he told a Jehovah’s Witness about Jesus being God?
faqs.answer: He says he asked, “how do you account for John 1:1,” and that the Word is God and the Word became flesh, and that Jesus’ name Emmanuel means “God with us.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

faqs.question: Does he say the Bible has errors?
faqs.answer: He says the rooster crowing twice or three times and a king being 8 or 18 years old “doesn’t take away from the truths of the Bible,” and says he can explain everything atheists call a contradiction.

faqs.question: What does he say about marriage in heaven?
faqs.answer: He says the Bible “plainly” says that in the age to come people neither marry nor are given in marriage, and that Jesus said people err “not knowing the scriptures nor the power of God.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels of God in heaven.

faqs.question: What does he say about infant baptism?
faqs.answer: He says “there is no infant baptism in the Bible” and that a baby cannot understand preaching or repent, since repentance comes before baptism.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then Peter said to them, “Repent, and let every one of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins; and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.

faqs.question: What does he say to people who say “don’t judge”?
faqs.answer: He says when they say homosexuality is okay they are making a judgment, “doing the very thing you’re telling me not to do,” and that he can decide “with the authority of the Bible.”

faqs.question: What does he say about turning the other cheek?
faqs.answer: He says “ain’t no time to turn no cheek, it’s a time to talk,” and that these people “need to be told, because God wants to save them.”

faqs.question: Does he say grace is something we grow in?
faqs.answer: He reads 2 Peter 3:17-18, that we should beware being led away by the error of the wicked and “grow in grace,” and says “grace is something you grow in.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: You therefore, beloved, since you know this beforehand, beware lest you also fall from your own steadfastness, being led away with the error of the wicked;

faqs.question: Does he say we can interpret scripture ourselves?
faqs.answer: He says “nobody has the right to interpret scripture… the Bible interprets, explains itself,” and you should find where else the Bible says it.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And beginning at Moses and all the Prophets, He expounded to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning Himself.

faqs.question: What does he say about magic ceremonies?
faqs.answer: He says “ain’t no magical ceremony,” and that “it’s the truth that sets you free… that causes you to grow… that heals you.”

faqs.question: What does he say about refusing medicine?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus said the sick need a doctor, that children die when parents refuse medicine, and that faith in your faith is wrong: “our faith is to be in the Lord Jesus Christ.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: When Jesus heard that, He said to them, “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick.
